question: Is it OK to take a census?
summary: Exodus 30 and Numbers 1, 3, and 26 have YHWH explicitly commanding Moses to take multiple censuses of Israel — the Sinai census, the Levite census, the firstborn census, the Moab census. 2 Samuel 24 and 1 Chronicles 21 have David taking a census and YHWH killing 70,000 people in response. Either censuses are commanded by God or they are sin provoking divine slaughter — both cannot be true at once.

reconcile.connective: Defenders draw a line between act and motive: the census itself was lawful and even commanded; David's guilt lay in numbering without God's order and out of pride.

discrepancy.connective: The objection is pressed by Steve Wells, who catalogues this as a standing contradiction — God commands censuses in the Torah, yet the same act under David provokes a plague that kills seventy thousand, a punishment Wells notes even David sees as unjust.

pd_work.note: Treats this exact tension at the passage: distinguishes the lawful, God-authorized census (Moses) from David's unauthorized, pride-driven numbering, resolving the 'commanded vs. sin' conflict on motive and sanction.

link.title: GotQuestions: Why was God so angry at David for taking the census?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment that frames Exodus 30 / Numbers as God-commanded and David's count as unauthorized and lacking the ransom provision.

excerpts.excerpt_text: The act of numbering the people was not in itself sinful; for Moses did it by the express authority of God. But David acted not only independently of such order or sanction, but from motives unworthy of the delegated king of Israel; from pride and vainglory; from self-confidence and distrust of God; and, above all, from ambitious designs of conquest …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly states the harmonizing distinction this contradiction turns on: numbering per se is not sinful (Moses did it by God's authority); David's sin was acting without that sanction and from unworthy motives. Strongest, most explicit reconcile voice on the row.
excerpts.source_note_text:
HE, HAVING THREE PLAGUES PROPOUNDED BY GAD, REPENTS, AND CHOOSES THREE DAYS' PESTILENCE. (Sa2 24:10-14)
David's heart smote him after that he had numbered the people. And David said unto the Lord, I have sinned--The act of numbering the people was not in itself sinful; for Moses did it by the express authority of God. But David acted not only independently of such order or sanction, but from motives unworthy of the delegated king of Israel; from pride and vainglory; from self-confidence and distrust of God; and, above all, from ambitious designs of conquest, in furtherance of which he was determined to force the people into military service, and to ascertain whether he could muster an army sufficient for the magnitude of the enterprises he contemplated. It was a breach of the constitution, an infringement of the liberties of the people, and opposed to that divine policy which required that Israel should continue a separate people. His eyes were not opened to the heinousness of his sin till God had spoken unto him by His commissioned prophet.
